body:
### Description

Fixes #14371

When running `gh pr checks` on a pull request where a check run has been re-queued, the command previously reported the previous run's conclusion (e.g. `pass`) and exited with code `0`, instead of reporting the re-queued run as `pending` (exit code `8`).

### Root Cause

In `pkg/cmd/pr/checks/aggregate.go`, `eliminateDuplicates` sorted check runs with:
```go
sort.Slice(checkContexts, func(i, j int) bool { return checkContexts[i].StartedAt.After(checkContexts[j].StartedAt) })
```
A check run that is queued and has not started yet has a zero-value `StartedAt`. Since `time.Time{}.After(startedAt)` evaluates to `false`, the unstarted re-run was sorted as older than the completed run. When deduplicating by check identifier, the completed run was kept, masking the pending re-run.

### Solution

1. Added `checkStartTime` helper in `pkg/cmd/pr/checks/aggregate.go` to extract the effective timestamp (`StartedAt` for `CheckRun`, or `CreatedAt` for `StatusContext`).
2. Updated `eliminateDuplicates` to use `sort.SliceStable` and rank unstarted/queued runs (`StartedAt.IsZero()`) ahead of completed runs, while preserving descending order for started runs.
3. Added unit tests in `pkg/cmd/pr/checks/checks_test.go` (`TestEliminateDuplicates`) covering re-queued check runs superseding completed runs in both input orders.

### Note for maintainers

@cli/code-reviewers: Issue #14371 is a triaged P2 bug verified by `cli-triage`. Requesting maintainer review and addition of the `help wanted` label so this PR meets automated screening requirements.
title: pr checks: prioritize re-queued check runs in eliminateDuplicates (#14371)
